findings.text: Log line reader advances a dump cursor over retained kernel messages and either fills a caller buffer with formatted text or reports only the size that would be produced, succeeding only when a valid record exists at the cursor and always reporting the produced length when requested.
Dump rewinder positions a dump cursor at the oldest retained sequence and records the current end sequence so a later scan starts from retained history.
Metadata reader exposes validity, summary info and line count for a given sequence without copying message text, delegating to a shared validity helper.
Command unregister operation detaches a previously registered debugger command descriptor from the global command list.

Debugger verbs for resuming execution, showing registers, changing a register and showing an exception frame are dispatched through the central command table; each handler validates its argument count before acting and reports debugger specific status.

Task and processor verbs for listing tasks, selecting current task, reporting or switching processor, entering remote debug mode and signalling a task are dispatched through the central table; processor selection validates range and responsiveness before requesting a switch.

System information verbs for summary, per processor variable display, kernel log display, environment display, help, system request invocation and pipe help are dispatched through the central table with usage hints, descriptions and enablement flags controlling when each may run.

Resume verb may run only on the processor that entered the debugger; otherwise it asks the operator to switch processors and fails with a processor number error. With no address it proceeds, with one address it parses the address, and with more it fails for argument count.

Register display first validates register availability, then formats each architectural register according to its width with increasing hexadecimal digits, wrapping near eighty columns; when the platform defines no registers it delegates to a platform dump routine. Register modify requires a name and value, tolerates a leading percent, resolves the name case sensitively, and writes the value narrowed to the defined width.

Log display accepts an optional line count and an optional offset, disables the LOGGING environment setting while running, counts available lines, then selects a window: negative counts select from an offset, positive counts select trailing lines before an offset, and zero selects everything, emitting notices when the buffer holds fewer lines than requested.

Log cursor reads are clamped forward to the oldest retained sequence before access, so cleared history is never returned; a successful read advances the cursor past the record just consumed. Size only probes use record metadata and line counts rather than copying text.

Printable size of a log record equals the per line prefix length multiplied by the number of text lines plus the stored text length plus one trailing newline; embedded newlines are already present in the stored text.

Processor status scan classifies each possible processor as offline, online but nonresponsive, idle, or responsive, then coalesces consecutive processors sharing a classification into ranges and omits a trailing all offline range. Processor switch with no argument only reports status; with one argument it parses the number and rejects out of range or nonresponsive targets before requesting the switch.

Task list output first shows the active task on each online processor and then all threads, each filtered by an optional state mask or environment default, with a fixed header; the scan aborts promptly if an interrupt flag is set.

Task selection accepts either a reset token meaning the entry processor task or a numeric identifier resolved in the initial namespace, reporting when absent and otherwise making the task current before announcing it. Termination verb requires a negative signal number and positive identifier, validates the signal, reports invalid inputs, resolves the thread to its group leader, and delivers the signal.

System summary requires no arguments and reports naming, release, version, machine, node, domain, wall time with timezone offset, uptime with day handling, three load averages split into integer and fractional parts, and memory totals scaled to kilobytes. Uptime derives from monotonic time converted to seconds and process count derives from thread count minus one.

Per processor display requires a symbol address with optional width and processor filter, defaults width to the debugger word size and rejects widths above it, validates that a selected processor is online, then for each online processor computes the instance address using the platform per processor base and reads the requested width, reporting unreadable instances and continuing.

System request verb requires exactly one key argument, derives a mask check from whether all commands are enabled, brackets the invocation with an incremented printk trap counter, and always reports success.

Help iterates the command list and shows only commands permitted by current enablement, aborting on interrupt, and wraps descriptions whose usage exceeds twenty characters onto a continuation line for readability.

Exception frame verb requires one address argument, resolves it through the generic address parser, and displays the register frame found at that address. Environment verb prints all variables and additionally reveals the debug mask when mask debugging is active.
Private debugger header is protected against multiple inclusion by a conventional guard macro.
Retained sequence is sampled without holding a lock by repeatedly reading a latch counter, selecting one of two slots, and retrying until the counter proves the read was stable.

Dump cursor carries at least a current sequence and a next sequence; rewind initializes the former from retained history and the latter from the ring next position, while line reads clamp and then advance the current position.
Each command table row associates a name with a handler, a short usage hint, a one line description, an optional minimum unique abbreviation length, and a bitmask of enablement and repeat properties.

System information collection observed here populates uptime in seconds, three load values, a process count, and memory statistics later rendered in kilobytes; the caller zeroes the structure before filling it.

Resume under catastrophic state announces the condition and current continuation policy: policy zero requires the verb to be issued twice before proceeding, policy two forces an immediate reboot, and other policies attempt to continue; the non reboot paths return a resume request to the outer loop.

Log display follows a count, compute skip, rewind, then emit sequence: it first counts lines, derives skip and count from sign and offset, rewinds, then skips and prints while honoring interrupt and stopping after the requested count.
Special negative return codes drive the outer debugger loop: one requests resumption, one requests a processor switch to a previously stored target, and one requests entry to remote debug mode.
Register modification parses a full sixty four bit value and then narrows it to eight, sixteen or thirty two bits for smaller registers, silently discarding high bits.
Log display has a global side effect: if the LOGGING variable is set it is forced to zero before reading, changing later logging behavior.
Signal delivery resolves the named thread to its process group leader, so the signal targets the whole process rather than the specific thread identifier supplied.
Per processor reads that fail report the processor, address and diagnostic status but do not abort the scan; remaining processors are still examined.
Kilobyte scaling shifts raw page counts left by page shift minus ten, which presumes a page size of at least one kilobyte and can overflow silently for very large counts.

Debugger loop control codes are negative integers: resume is minus one thousand one, processor switch minus one thousand two, single step minus one thousand three, and remote debug entry minus one thousand five.

Debug flag values are two for breakpoint, four for summary block analysis, eight for generic activation record, sixteen for arch activation record, thirty two for full block analysis, sixty four for state, mask sixty five thousand five hundred thirty five, and shift sixteen.

Thirty two bit platform defaults declare four bytes per word; register and virtual addresses render as hexadecimal with leading zero x, with fixed width zero padded variants, and file counts render as decimal.
